<p class="print-note">Print this page. Two sheets per team, cut apart. Page 1
is the checklist, filled and signed in session B of meeting&nbsp;4 and handed
in. Page 2 carries the shared card and six practice cards. Nine copies of each
plus three spares, in the lettered envelopes before class.</p>

<div class="sheet">

  <div class="sheethead">
    <h2>The cards</h2>
    <div class="id">Team <span class="fill w08"></span> &nbsp; Date <span class="fill w16"></span></div>
  </div>

  <div class="instr">
    <p><span class="lead">Session B, read once at 3:41.</span> Check in first, nine minutes, one sheet per team, as every week.</p>
    <p>Then the shared card, in the red box. Three answers on paper, five minutes. Which gate does this trip: the IRB, a data-use agreement, terms of service, a conflict of interest, integrity, or none? What is the earliest date it has to start? And the half that carries the marks: what is the version of this project that is legal, is honest, and is still worth doing? I tell the answer once.</p>
    <p>Then your own project on the checklist, twelve minutes. Every member signs. Then every team at the front in letter order, two and a half minutes each with a hard stop. One of you reads the gate rows and the two bottom lines. The room names a gate you missed. I rule. A team that trips nothing says so.</p>
    <p>The six other cards are practice. Their answers appear on the meeting page on Thursday.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card shared">
    <span class="num">Shared card</span>
    <p class="txt">A team holds a licensed WRDS extract and is about to upload it to a chatbot for cleaning.</p>
    <p class="q">Gate · earliest start · the honest version</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card">

  </div>
